## The maximal lactate accumulation rate (VLamax)

VLamax comes from its own test, a short all-out sprint, not from the step test:

$$VLamax = \frac{La_{peak} - La_{pre}}{t_{test} - t_{alactic}}$$

Take a lactate sample before the sprint and every minute for several minutes after it; the highest value is the
peak. `vlamax()` does the arithmetic:

```{r}
vlamax(lactate_pre = 1.1, lactate_post = c(8.9, 10.4, 10.9, 10.6, 10.1), test_duration = 15)
```

The alactic time is the part of the sprint assumed to be covered by phosphocreatine. In 50 cyclists, fixing it at
3.5 s gave the most reliable VLamax (ICC 0.91, CV 3.1%), while estimating it from the power curve did not (CV 12-26%);
a 1-s change in it can change VLamax by up to 26% (Meixner et al., 2024). Protocols differ widely between studies
(Langley et al., 2025), and whether VLamax measures the maximal glycolytic rate is still debated: in 11 cyclists it
added little beyond the power of the sprint itself (Clark & Macdermid, 2025). Compare VLamax only within the same
protocol, ergometer and analyzer.

## References

Clark B, Macdermid PW. VLamax correlates strongly with glycolytic performance. Res Q Exerc Sport. 2025:1-8.

vLamax: a systematic review. J Sci Cycling. 2025;14(1):9. doi:10.28985/1425.jsc.09

Meixner B, Nusser V, Koehler K, Sablain M, Boone J, Sperlich B. Reliability of power output, maximal rate of capillary
blood lactate accumulation, and phosphagen contribution time following 15-s sprint cycling in amateur cyclists.
Physiol Rep. 2024;12(10):e16086. doi:10.14814/phy2.16086
